challenges.name: background-tasks-quiz
challenges.title: Read the battery complaints
challenges.description: Three statements about what Rice Rocket found when couriers complained that the app drained their battery and still showed stale deliveries. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: Who decides when a background task runs on Android and iOS: your code, or the operating system's scheduler? What does a "minimum" interval promise?
Compare what wakes the GPS: an update every second at the highest accuracy, or an update only after the courier moved some distance.
Think about what happens to the JavaScript runtime when the app goes to the background and the OS suspends it.

questions.question:
The sync was registered as a background task:

```ts
await BackgroundTask.registerTaskAsync("sync-outbox", { minimumInterval: 1 }); // minutes
```

```text
adb logcat (2 hours, phone idle in a pocket)
10:02 sync-outbox ran
10:19 sync-outbox ran
10:51 sync-outbox ran
11:40 sync-outbox ran
```

Statement: "`minimumInterval: 1` makes the operating system run the sync every minute; the gaps in the log mean the task registration is broken."
questions.explanation: False. Background tasks are scheduled by the OS (WorkManager on Android, BGTaskScheduler on iOS): the interval is a lower bound, not a schedule. Android's periodic work does not run more often than every 15 minutes, and both systems delay work further for battery saving, Doze and app usage patterns. The log shows a working registration. Anything that must happen within seconds needs the app in the foreground or a push from the server.

True. Continuous high-accuracy GPS is one of the most expensive things a phone does. A distance interval sends an update only after the courier actually moved, and a balanced accuracy lets the OS use cheaper sources when they are good enough. Dispatch needs a position every few dozen meters, not every second at standstill.

False. When the app is backgrounded the OS suspends it shortly after, and JavaScript timers stop with it; they resume only when the app comes back (or a background task wakes it). Retries in the background belong in a scheduled background task, and the reliable moment to flush the outbox is when the app returns to the foreground or the network comes back while it runs.
